7. Investment Strategy The investment objective of the Scheme is to generate capital appreciation / income from a portfolio, predominantly of equity & equity related instruments. The Scheme would predominantly invest in companies spanning entire market capitalization that: a) are likely to achieve above average growth b) enjoy distinct competitive advantages, and c) have superior financial strength. The aim of the equity strategy will be to build a portfolio, representing a cross section of companies diversified across major industries, economic sectors and market capitalization that offer an acceptable risk reward balance. A part of the funds may be invested in debt and money market instruments. Investment in Debt securities (including securitised debt) and Money Market Instruments will be as per the limits in the asset allocation table of the Scheme, subject to permissible limits laid under SEBI (MF) Regulations. Investment

Investment in Debt securities (including securitised debt) and Money Market Instruments will be as per the limits in the asset allocation table of the Scheme, subject to permissible limits laid under SEBI (MF) Regulations. Investment in debt securities will be guided by credit quality, liquidity, interest rates and their outlook. The Scheme may also invest in the hybrid securities viz. units of REITs and InvITs for diversification and subject to necessary stipulations by SEBI from time to time. Subject to the Regulations and the applicable guidelines, the Scheme may engage in Stock Lending activities. The Scheme may also invest in the schemes of Mutual Funds in terms of the prevailing SEBI (MF) Regulations. (v) Risk factors associated with investment in Tri-Party Repo The mutual fund is a member of securities segment and Triparty Repo trade settlement of the Clearing Corporation of India (CCIL). All transactions of the mutual fund in government securities and in Tri-party Repo trades

The mutual fund is a member of securities segment and Triparty Repo trade settlement of the Clearing Corporation of India (CCIL). All transactions of the mutual fund in government securities and in Tri-party Repo trades are settled centrally through the infrastructure and settlement systems provided by CCIL; Thus, reducing the settlement and counterparty risks considerably for transactions in the said segments. The members are required to contribute an amount as communicated by CCIL from time to time to the default fund maintained by CCIL as a part of the default waterfall (a loss mitigating measure of CCIL in case of default by any member in settling transactions routed through CCIL). As per the waterfall mechanism, after the defaulter's margins and the defaulter's contribution to the default fund have been appropriated, CCIL's contribution is used to meet the losses. (xv) Risk factors associated with Repo in permitted Corporate Debt Securities In repo transactions, also known as a repo or sale repurchase agreement, securities are sold with the seller agreeing to buy them back at later date. Some of the risks associated with repo in corporate debt are given below: Counterparty Risk: Counterparty risk refers to the inability of the seller to meet the obligation to buy back securities at the contracted price on the contracted date. In case of over the counter (OTC) repo trades, the

Counterparty risk refers to the inability of the seller to meet the obligation to buy back securities at the contracted price on the contracted date. Investors are issued rated Pass Through Certificates (PTCs), the proceeds of which are paid as consideration to the originator. In this manner, the originator, by selling 40 HDFC Large Cap Fund-SID

his loan receivables to an SPV, receives consideration from investors much before the maturity of the underlying loans. Investors are paid from the collections of the underlying loans from borrowers. Typically, the transaction is provided with a limited amount of credit enhancement (as stipulated by the rating agency for a target rating), which provides protection to investors against defaults by the underlying borrowers. (v) Risk factors associated with investment in Tri-Party Repo The mutual fund is a member of securities segment and Triparty Repo trade settlement of the Clearing Corporation of India (CCIL). All transactions of the mutual fund in government securities and in Tri-party Repo trades are settled centrally through the infrastructure and settlement systems provided by CCIL; Thus, reducing the settlement and counterparty risks considerably for transactions in the said segments. reducing the settlement and counterparty risks considerably for transactions in the said segments. The members are required to contribute an amount as communicated by CCIL from time to time to the default fund maintained by CCIL as a part of the default waterfall (a loss mitigating measure of CCIL in case of default by any member in settling transactions routed through CCIL). # HDFC MF - Request Statement (snapshot, captured 2026-11-12) Source: https://www.hdfcfund.com/services/additional-info/request-statement HDFC Mutual Fund can email an account statement to the investor's registered email ID. After the first investment, an allotment confirmation is sent by email and/or SMS within 5 business days to investors who have registered an email or mobile number. A Consolidated Account Statement (CAS) is sent on or before the 10th of the month following any month in which the folio had transactions. On a specific request, the fund provides an account statement within 5 business days. The Request Statement page links to: Account statement (HDFC MF Download Statement page); Dividend statement, Exit load statement and Capital Gains Statement (HDFC MF investor portal, investor-web.hdfcfund.com); Consolidated account statement and Consolidated realized gains statement (CAMS online). An account statement can also be requested by SMS, through the IVR on

Exit load statement and Capital Gains Statement (HDFC MF investor portal, investor-web.hdfcfund.com); Consolidated account statement and Consolidated realized gains statement (CAMS online). An account statement can also be requested by SMS, through the IVR on the toll-free number 1800-3010-6767 or 1800-419-7676, or at any HDFC MF Investor Service Centre.

# HDFC MF - Download Statement (snapshot, captured 2026-11-12) Source: https://www.hdfcfund.com/services/consolidated-account-statement To download an account statement on HDFC MF's Download Statement page, the investor enters a PAN or a folio number, verifies with an OTP, selects the duration (for example the current financial year) and the statement is sent by email. An Account Statement summarises all mutual fund transactions in the folio, including purchases, redemptions, switches, dividends and units allotted. The statement can be downloaded as soon as the investor begins investing. There is no charge or fee for receiving or downloading the Account Statement. Two types are available: a PAN-based account statement covering all folios linked to the PAN, and a folio-based account statement for a single folio.

# HDFC MF - How to get a capital gain statement (snapshot, page dated 2025-08-12) Source: https://www.hdfcfund.com/learn/blog/how-get-capital-gain-statement-mutual-fund-schemes-india A capital gain statement reports gains or losses from redeeming mutual fund units during a period, split into short-term and long-term gains, and is used when filing an income tax return. It can be obtained from the registrar and transfer agents (CAMS or KFintech) using the PAN and registered email ID, from the AMC's own website, or from investment platforms in their tax or reports section. A Consolidated Account Statement in capital-gains format covers redemptions across all mutual fund schemes linked to the PAN. Most registrars and platforms provide the capital gain statement free of cost.

# HDFC MF - SIP FAQs (snapshot, captured 2026-11-12) Source: https://www.hdfcfund.com/services/faqs/systematic-investment-plan HDFC MF's SIP FAQ notes that many AMCs allow an SIP to start from Rs. 100 in most schemes, subject to the restrictions in each scheme's Scheme Information Document, and that the commonly cited minimum is Rs. 500. The scheme-specific minimum SIP amount should be checked in the scheme's KIM, SID or Scheme Summary Document.

Getting to Know Mutual Funds What is a Mutual Fund? A mutual fund is a collective investment option where money from multiple investors like you is pooled together and invested across equity, money market instruments and other liquid instruments, gold and silver instruments and in invITs. This pooled money is managed by professional fund managers, who invest it according to the scheme’s investment objective, and you must make sure it aligns with your own investment goals as well. Wondering why you should invest in Mutual Funds? Mutual funds allow you to invest in a wide range of assets such as equity, money market instruments and other liquid instruments, gold and silver instruments and in invITs. They provide an opportunity for retail investors like you to participate in capital markets without having to manage investments on your own. Over the long

Common Terms related to Mutual Fund Investing What is NAV? NAV (Net Asset Value) is the price of one unit of a mutual fund. It is calculated at the end of each trading day after market closes by subtracting total liabilities from total assets and dividing by outstanding units; it is the price you pay to buy or redeem units, subject to applicable cut-off times and regulatory conditions. What is Base expense ratio? Base Expense Ratio (BER) refers to the core recurring expenses associated with managing and operating a mutual fund scheme. It is the sum of investment and advisory fees, marketing and selling expenses including fees, commission and charges towards distribution of mutual fund schemes if any, administrative and operating expenses and scheme servicing and recurring management costs. What is Total expense ratio? Total Expense Ratio (TER) represents the

including fees, commission and charges towards distribution of mutual fund schemes if any, administrative and operating expenses and scheme servicing and recurring management costs. What is Total expense ratio? Total Expense Ratio (TER) represents the complete cost of investing, which adds external costs like brokerage, transaction fees, and statutory levies to the base fee. TER = Base Expense Ratio (BER) + Brokerage Cost + Transaction Cost incurred for the purpose of execution of trade + Statutory levies (including GST) What is an Exit Load? Exit load is a fee charged when you redeem mutual fund units and is deducted from the NAV at the time of redemption. For instance, if the NAV is ₹100 and the exit load is 1%, the redemption price would be ₹99 per unit. applicable NAV for purchase/redemption is subject to applicable cut-off times and regulatory

What is Redemption? Redemption Redemption means withdrawing or selling your mutual fund units. When you redeem, your units are sold at the applicable NAV, and the proceeds are credited to your bank account. Depending on the scheme, an exit load or tax may apply, especially if you redeem before the specified period. Withdraw You can redeem your entire investment at once, or in parts, whenever and however much you need. SWP is simply a structured way to redeem, instead of withdrawing the full amount in one shot, it lets you set up regular, automatic partial redemptions. What is an SWP? A Systematic Withdrawal Plan (SWP) allows you to withdraw a fixed amount at regular intervals, such as monthly or quarterly from your mutual fund investment. Instead of redeeming the entire amount at once, SWP provides a steady income, making it

# AMFI Mutual Fund Sahi Hai - Glossary (snapshot, captured 2026-11-12) Source: https://www.mutualfundssahihai.com/en/glossary?page=1 The expense ratio, or Total Expense Ratio (TER), is the annual cost of running a scheme and has a direct bearing on its NAV: a lower expense ratio means a higher NAV, other things being equal. SEBI caps the TER that schemes can charge; fund-of-funds have separate limits depending on the underlying schemes. An exit load is a charge some schemes levy on redemptions made within a stipulated period, intended to discourage selling too soon. Exit load is a percentage applied on the NAV used for the redemption; with a 1% exit load you receive 99% of the redemption value if you exit within the stipulated period. Most schemes other than liquid funds charge an exit load for redemptions within the stipulated period.
